summary: Sequential uploader fanout causing unbalanced tenant quota exhaustion and opaque 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightAnalytics reports repeated 429s on bulk ingest job runs that are implemented as a short sequential uploader (single worker) which issues signed-url requests to a callback endpoint. The traffic pattern is serial but results in bursty upstream routing and tenant quota depletion.

Impact:
- Several production data pipelines failed to complete; downstream feature tables left in partial state.
- Customer observed 15-30% of job runs returning 429s mid-run, requiring retries and manual reconciliation.
- Customer is on Dedicated (monthly reserved capacity) and expects predictable throughput.

Environment:
- prod-us-west (dedicated pool: brightanalytics-prod)
- Ingest path: POST /v1/embeddings/batch -> callback signed-url fetches -> confirm endpoint -> finalization
- Model used for on-the-fly validation: redwood/opt-6.7b (light), not heavy compute at time of failure

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start job with N=5000 documents. Orchestrator issues signed-URL requests sequentially to edge callback (one after another).
2) Each signed-url fetch performs small payload upload then immediate confirm API call to Redwood: /v1/ingest/confirm (same API key).
3) After ~700-1200 sequential confirms the pipeline begins seeing 429 responses from the confirm endpoint; further confirms fail until a refill window passes.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses are returned with standard throttle headers X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining but Remaining is sometimes reported as 0 even when console shows credits left.
- Customer sees a sawtooth pattern: quiet then repeated mid-run throttles.
- Console token-usage graphs show multiple small spikes but do not attribute to a single route.

Customer-provided logs (redacted):
"2026-03-09T23:12:01Z confirm 200 id=abc123"
"2026-03-09T23:12:02Z confirm 200 id=abc124"
"..."
"2026-03-09T23:35:20Z confirm 429 id=abc899 message="quota_exhausted" x-rl-remaining=0 x-rl-limit=600"

Notes: The uploader is single-threaded (sequential) but invokes the confirm route repeatedly within sub-second intervals for hundreds of requests. Customer suspects a counting mismatch between health-checks / origin probes and the confirm route accounting when signed URLs are used.

Expected behavior:
- Sequential confirms should consume tokens smoothly against the tenant quota without abrupt mid-run 429s.

Requested from Support:
- Explain why sequential single-worker patterns trigger tenant quota exhaustion.
- Confirm whether signed-URL callbacks, preflight probes, or edge affinity are double-counting requests.
- Recommend immediate mitigations and longer-term best practice for dedicated customers to avoid these mid-run throttles.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Sofia Mendes (support): Case opened after BrightAnalytics reported 429 waves during nightly ingest. Assigned to Liam for initial triage.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Acknowledged. Requested request-id samples and their X-RateLimit headers. Asked customer to provide any proxy/ingress IPs used for uploader workers.

2026-03-10 12:40 - BrightAnalytics (customer): Provided sample request-ids and stacktrace for uploader (single worker). Confirmed no parallel workers are used. Provided edge IPs 34.217.12.9 and 34.217.12.11.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): We observed multiple confirm calls from two NATed IPs plus repeated health-check probes from the customer's orchestrator. Hypothesis: orchestrator health-checks + confirm calls are both counting against tenant refill window leading to faster burnout. Requested replication steps to temporarily disable health-checks.

2026-03-11 13:30 - Support (Sofia): Sent immediate mitigation: enable small delay (200ms) between confirms and enable exponential backoff on 429s. Also recommended a short pre-roll peak window expansion for dedicated pools while we investigate.
2026-03-12 07:18 - BrightAnalytics: Applied the delay and saw reduction in 429s but still encountering spikes at run boundaries. Asked whether signed-URL fetches trigger separate route accounting.
investigation_notes: Checked tenant refill logs for brightanalytics-prod: observed refill interval of 60s with burst bucket of 600 tokens. Multiple processes (orchestrator health probes, signed-url confirmation calls, and an internal telemetry heartbeat) were emitting requests in the same refill window leading to cumulative consumption exceeding bucket capacity.

Edge-proxy NAT reuse detected: two egress IPs from customer are mapping multiple uploader flows; proxy connection reuse sometimes causes HTTP/2 stream multiplexing which can result in preflight-like requests being recorded separately by the ingress counting layer.

Console shows discrepancy between tokens visible in UI and low-level accounting: UI aggregates per-minute buckets, while rate-limiter enforces per-second windows for confirm route which can cause temporary zero remaining even if minute-level quota remains.

No evidence of double-counting from Redwood side for signed-url contents; signed-url fetches to object-storage are external and not charged, but the confirm API calls are charged and are the primary consumer.
Related to SUP-401313 where keepalive and readiness probes were counted; recommended to check orchestrator readiness probe config.
suggested_workarounds: Add a 150-300ms jittered delay between sequential confirm calls to spread out consumption across refill windows.
Disable or reduce frequency of orchestrator health-checks that target the same tenant API key during large jobs.
Use batched confirm endpoints (if available) to amortize token cost per batch instead of per-item confirms.
Request a temporary burst increase for the dedicated pool while long-term config changes are validated (Support can coordinate with Capacity team).
resolution_notes: Triage ongoing. Customer applied a delay and observed partial improvement; we are coordinating with Capacity and Runtime teams to (1) confirm per-second vs per-minute accounting mismatch, (2) evaluate a short-lived burst expansion, and (3) produce a short best-practice guidance doc for sequential uploader patterns. Next action: SRE to run targeted trace on 2026-03-13 ingest window and return findings.
next_steps: SRE: enable detailed request tracing for brightanalytics-prod during next run (scheduled 2026-03-13 23:00 UTC).
Support: send guidance note for orchestrator health-check tuning and backoff implementation (by 2026-03-12 EOD).
Capacity: prepare a temporary burst lift request if traces confirm bucket exhaustion due to refill window misalignment.
